issues.legal_issue: An authority deciding a statutory review that may displace an existing mining lease acts quasi-judicially and must give the affected grantee a reasonable opportunity to be heard.
material_facts: A state government granted the appellant mining leases for five areas and delivered possession to him.
A competing applicant sought statutory review of the grants, and the reviewing authority cancelled the leases for two areas and directed that leases be granted to the competing applicant.
The reviewing authority made its decision without giving the appellant an opportunity to present his case, despite his request to be heard.
issues.conclusion: The reviewing authority acted quasi-judicially and was required to give the affected grantee a reasonable opportunity to represent his case. Because it did not do so, its order was quashed, with liberty to decide the review afresh after providing that opportunity.
issues.legal_principle: Under rules 52–55 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1949, made under section 6 of the Mines and Minerals (Regulation and Development) Act, 1941, a statutory review initiated by an aggrieved party creates a lis between that party and the grantee. The grant is effective unless displaced on review, so the grantee has an interest in the review’s outcome and a right to represent his case. Applying Province of Bombay v. Kushaldas S. Advani, which adopted the test in R. v. Electricity Commissioners, an authority determining contested rights under legal authority must act judicially unless the governing law indicates otherwise. The reviewing rules did not negate that duty; the failure to provide a reasonable opportunity to be heard therefore justified quashing the order.

rule.if: statutory_review_of_mining_lease and review_challenges_existing_grant and grantee_has_interest_in_outcome and not grantee_given_opportunity_to_be_heard

predicates.statutory_review_of_mining_lease: A reviewing authority is deciding a statutory review concerning a mining lease.
predicates.review_challenges_existing_grant: The review seeks to displace a lease already granted to another person.
predicates.grantee_has_interest_in_outcome: The existing grantee has an interest in the review because its decision may affect the grant.
predicates.grantee_given_opportunity_to_be_heard: The reviewing authority gave the affected grantee a reasonable opportunity to present their case.

issues.definition: When a statutory review challenges an existing mining-lease grant, the grantee has an interest in its outcome, and the grantee is not given an opportunity to be heard, the review order is quashed.
